storyboard.claim: A presentation disaster unfolds as equipment fails and the audience disconnects.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An anxious presenter sweating beside a malfunctioning slide projector in a boardroom.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the presentation nightmare scenario described in slide four.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visually grounds the physical embarrassment of the failing equipment in a professional setting.

storyboard.claim: Returning to the car in shock, catastrophic internal self-talk takes over.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hands clutching the steering wheel in a dark car as panic settles in.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The retreat from the meeting room to the isolation of the car.
storyboard.addedInformation: Highlights the visceral panic grip right before the negative monologue begins.

storyboard.claim: The mind instantly defaults to a permanent indictment of ability.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The speaker slumped in shame under the weight of an absolute self-judgment.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Speaks the internal sentence triggered in the car.
storyboard.addedInformation: Isolates the fatalist internal voice that turns an episode into an identity.

storyboard.claim: Permanent attribution stretches a single bad afternoon across an entire future.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seligman points to a timeline clock showing one event stretched indefinitely.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Diagnoses the cognitive distortion occurring in beat 82.
storyboard.addedInformation: Exposes how the brain unlawfully turns an isolated afternoon into a lifetime trait.

storyboard.claim: Contrasting permanent language with temporary framing reveals the core divergence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clean two-way sorter comparing permanent disaster language against timebound assessment.
storyboard.onScreenText: ALWAYS FAIL vs BLEW THIS ONE
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Provides the explicit linguistic contrast for the time dimension.
storyboard.addedInformation: Splits the fatalistic lifetime diagnosis from the specific single failure.

storyboard.claim: Viewing setbacks as permanent kills all drive before the day even ends.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A defeated worker lying paralyzed in bed under an immovable boulder of fatalism.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the immediate behavioral consequence of permanent attribution.
storyboard.addedInformation: Depicts bedtime paralysis where resignation replaces any plan to adapt.

storyboard.claim: Believing a flaw is permanent makes practicing in front of a mirror feel futile.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A person standing numbly turned away from a practice mirror, unwilling to rehearse.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Illustrates why permanent explanations destroy the incentive to practice.
storyboard.addedInformation: Reveals the mirror not as vanity but as an abandoned training tool.

storyboard.claim: This self-fulfilling prophecy aligns with Bernard Weiner's attribution theory.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seligman holding Weiner's academic volume on causal attribution in an academic study.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Connects personal psychology to formal behavioral science.
storyboard.addedInformation: Grounds the self-fulfilling spiral in validated psychological literature.

storyboard.claim: Weiner examined the partial reinforcement extinction effect, known as the slot machine effect.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A mechanical lever game symbol representing erratic intermittent payoffs.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the behavioral mechanism underlying extinction persistence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Translates the technical PRE acronym into the recognizable gamble paradigm.

storyboard.claim: In continuous reinforcement, stopping rewards causes subjects to quit immediately.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Maier demonstrating an operant chamber lever where food delivery has abruptly halted.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Establishes the baseline continuous reinforcement extinction condition.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visualizes the animal laboratory baseline before introducing partial reward.

storyboard.claim: A sharp contrast in rewards leads to rapid abandonment of the behavior.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Maier pointing to the inactive lever apparatus where effort ceases at once.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the animal's swift realization when 100 percent payout stops.
storyboard.addedInformation: Emphasizes how obvious predictability makes quitting an instant choice.

storyboard.claim: Rewarding only occasional attempts builds resistance to extinction.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Solomon observing intermittent schedule records charting sporadic reinforcement.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the contrasting schedule of variable rewards.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the experimental schedule that conditions persistence through dry spells.

storyboard.claim: Conditioned by unrewarded stretches, the subject presses a hundred times before quitting.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Solomon pointing to a tall tally of unrewarded lever presses on an apparatus.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Details the extreme tenacity generated by partial schedules.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the stubborn endurance built by irregular reward history.

storyboard.claim: Humans break the classic behavioral rule through cognitive interpretation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seligman presenting human trial anomalies that contradict pure conditioning models.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transitions from animal behavioral conditioning to human cognitive override.
storyboard.addedInformation: Marks the breakdown of strict behaviorism when applied to human minds.

storyboard.claim: Belief in a permanent cause causes humans to quit immediately despite past partial reinforcement.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clean causal flow linking belief in permanent failure directly to sudden surrender.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the cognitive switch that short-circuits animal conditioning.
storyboard.addedInformation: Demonstrates belief overriding thousands of reinforced repetitions.

storyboard.claim: Assuming someone permanently disabled your machine access ends effort on the spot.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A frustrated office worker glaring at a silent espresso maker, assuming hostile sabotage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Grounds the theory in an everyday office appliance scenario.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrasts personal permanent hostility with simple mechanical trouble.

storyboard.claim: Concluding the machine is only temporarily jammed keeps you jiggling the handle.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The worker patiently working the machine lever, believing persistence will dislodge the jam.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Provides the optimistic alternative interpretation of the same broken appliance.
storyboard.addedInformation: Illustrates how temporary framing preserves mechanical and mental initiative.

storyboard.claim: The internal explanation of permanent versus temporary acts as the master switch for resilience.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A balance scale weighing permanent against temporary explanations as a decisive pivot.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarizes the decisive role of the permanence dimension.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames temporal attribution as the core mechanism controlling persistent action.

storyboard.claim: What if poor public speaking is an objective reality with shaking voice and slouching posture?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A nervous speaker at a podium with trembling hands and slumped shoulders.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The host raises a devil's advocate objection about objective incompetence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives concrete voice to the fear that optimism is merely sugarcoated delusion.

storyboard.claim: Labeling a glaring failure as a permanent flaw feels like rigorous self-honesty.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An introspective worker questioning whether harsh self-judgment is just realism.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Deepens the challenge: isn't permanent labeling simply facing facts?
storyboard.addedInformation: Addresses the common misconception that pessimism equals unvarnished truth.

storyboard.claim: Calling a disaster a temporary glitch sounds to skeptics like outright delusion.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host challenging whether calling severe failure temporary is just denial.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pushes the objection to its sharpest critique: optimism as self-deception.
storyboard.addedInformation: Validates the viewer's natural skepticism before delivering Seligman's distinction.

storyboard.claim: Telling people to lie to themselves just to keep a sunny disposition seems dangerous.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host holding up a hollow smiling theatrical mask representing fake positivity.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the hazard of toxic positive platitudes.
storyboard.addedInformation: Uses the mask to reject superficial cheerleading in favor of cognitive realism.

storyboard.claim: Acknowledging a real skill deficit does not require a permanent explanation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seligman pointing toward a training target, separating capability from permanence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Seligman directly resolves the objection raised by the host.
storyboard.addedInformation: Dismantles the false choice between honest appraisal and permanent surrender.

storyboard.claim: Pointing to timebound causes is completely realistic and actionable.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seligman explaining how attributing poor performance to timebound factors preserves agency.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Proposes the timebound attribution as true realism.
storyboard.addedInformation: Clarifies that optimism changes the time horizon, not the objective facts.

storyboard.claim: Admitting you underprepared or lacked rehearsal is an honest, timebound judgment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A presenter reviewing thin presentation notes, identifying specific preparation gaps.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives concrete examples of timebound, fixable self-critiques.
storyboard.addedInformation: Replaces vague personal inadequacy with specific missing preparation steps.

storyboard.claim: Critiques like poor client research are brutally honest assessments, but strictly temporary.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A professional analyzing meeting data at a desk, facing hard facts without self-pity.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reiterates that rigorous criticism does not require permanent damnation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows a focused professional diagnosing correctable errors calmly.

storyboard.claim: Temporary causes yield actionable tasks, whereas claiming innate flaw paralyzes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow comparing an actionable repair path with a dead-end permanent trait label.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts the functional output of both explanatory habits.
storyboard.addedInformation: Highlights how temporary framing immediately generates constructive work.

storyboard.claim: Belief in genetic incompetence binds and paralyzes you despite having zero scientific basis.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A professional bound by psychological chains of fatalistic genetics, immobilized.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the paralyzing effect of false genetic determinism.
storyboard.addedInformation: Depicts mental chains forged by erroneous claims of fixed ineptitude.

storyboard.claim: Your explanatory habit dictates exactly how long you stay helpless after defeat.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seligman holding an hourglass showing the finite duration of timebound helplessness.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Defines helplessness recovery speed as a direct function of permanence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Uses the hourglass to represent time passing back into effective initiative.

storyboard.claim: Viewing causes as timebound fuels the energy to practice and master skills.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A rejuvenated speaker rehearsing with renewed focus and energetic posture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Delivers the positive resolution of timebound thinking.
storyboard.addedInformation: Replaces earlier paralysis with deliberate, motivated rehearsal.

storyboard.claim: Permanent attributions demand surrender, closing the door on progress.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host pointing at a closed door labeled with absolute finality as transition to space.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the time dimension chapter and pivots toward the spatial dimension.
storyboard.addedInformation: Draws the firm boundary between permanence and the new concept of pervasiveness.

storyboard.claim: The second pillar addresses what happens when defeat bleeds beyond its original boundary.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seligman gesturing to branching fracture lines spreading across distinct domains.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Formally introduces the second explanatory pillar: pervasiveness.
storyboard.addedInformation: Illustrates contamination spreading from work into all life domains.

storyboard.claim: Passed over for a hoped-for promotion, an employee walks to the elevator in shock.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A disappointed worker carrying a briefcase toward office elevators after rejection.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the promotion rejection scenario for pervasiveness.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets the concrete scene of an evening corporate departure after bad news.

storyboard.claim: The internal monologue escalates from a lost promotion to total life and relationship failure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The worker slumped on the commute home, swallowed by catastrophic universal panic.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Tracks the rapid escalation from professional loss to relationship doom.
storyboard.addedInformation: Depicts universal catastrophizing expanding across unrelated life spheres.

storyboard.claim: An optimistic explanatory style constructs a protective firewall around setbacks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seligman indicating a protective barrier shield that contains workplace damage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the defensive cognitive architecture of optimistic pervasiveness.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the central firewall metaphor that isolates discrete setbacks.

storyboard.claim: The optimist confines failure to specific parameters like competitor database experience.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A job candidate objectively recognizing that an external applicant had specific technical qualifications.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Provides the optimistic internal dialogue containing the promotion rejection.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows realistic competence attribution replacing sweeping existential shame.

storyboard.claim: By containing failure to the office, the rest of life stays functional and enjoyable.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The professional sitting peacefully at home having dinner with family despite workplace setbacks.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Demonstrates the practical life benefit of a strong mental firewall.
storyboard.addedInformation: Proves that specific attribution protects evening home life and relationships.

storyboard.claim: Seligman's research features a definitive study of two laid-off accountants, Nora and Kevin.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Nora and Kevin standing in their corporate accounting department before the layoff.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the book's landmark comparative case study.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes both protagonists in the same workplace before testing pervasiveness.

storyboard.claim: Both worked at the exact same firm and were let go during a massive corporate downsizing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Nora and Kevin carrying boxes and briefcases out through office doors together.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Applies the identical objective adversity to both subjects.
storyboard.addedInformation: Controls for external severity: identical firm, identical downsizing event.

storyboard.claim: Both Nora and Kevin registered high permanence scores, expecting a prolonged poor job market.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Nora and Kevin looking out somberly at economic charts predicting prolonged unemployment.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reveals that both shared the exact same bleak time horizon.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows their equal vulnerability on the permanence axis before pervasiveness splits them.
